Sāyaṇācārya
brother of Mādhavācārya an. Bhoganātha, son of Māyaṇa, wrote under Vīrabukkabhūpāla I of Vidyānagara (1350-79) an. his successor Harihara. He died in 1387.
His numerous works are attributed by turn to himself, to his brother Mādhava or Vidyāraṇya. He was disciple of Viṣṇusarvajña an. Śaṅkarānanda; preceptor of Rāmakṛṣṇa (a of C. on Pañcadaśī). There can be very little doubt an. thorough examination proves that his comments on Ṛgveda an. Taittirīyasaṃhitā were only partially done by himself an. carried on by his followers. The interpretation of Taittirīyabrāhmaṇa, Taittirīy- [Page333-a. āraṇyaka, Aitareyāraṇyaka shows a want of description which can only be explained on the supposition that their authorship belongs to a different writer.
Q. by Vidyāraṇya of Vijayanagara in his Rājakālanirṇaya, MD. 12772; by Keladi Veṅkaṭādrināyaka in his C. on Śivagītā, BBRAS. 1002; ment. in Darśapaurṇamāsaprāyaścitta, Bomb. Uni. 822 an. also by many more authorities.
For Sāyaṇa's equipment of Pūrvamīmāṃsā, a study based on Sāyaṇa's introduction to the Ṛgveda, see S. G. Moghe, J. of Ori. Inst. M. S. Uni. Baroda XXIV. p.. 257ff.
For more ref. on the author an. his works, see M. Kripacharyalu, Sāyaṇa an. Mādhava Vidyāraṇya: A Study of their lives an. letters, Rajyalakshmi Publications, Guntur, 1986.
For the ref. about his identity an. his relationship with Mādhavācārya an. Vidyāraṇya, see under Mādhavācārya an. also under Vidyāraṇya
